title: Cambricon-M: A Fibonacci-Coded Charge-Domain SRAM-Based CIM Accelerator for DNN Inference
problem: High-resolution ADCs dominate energy consumption (up to 64%) in charge-domain SRAM-based CIM architectures because wide ranges of input analog values require high precision conversion to high-bitwidth digital data. This ADC overhead significantly limits energy efficiency for DNN inference.
motivation: Reducing ADC energy overhead substantially improves overall energy efficiency of compute-in-memory accelerators, making them more practical for deployment.
method: Cambricon-M applies Fibonacci coding (a constraint ensuring that whenever a bit is '1', its neighboring bits must be '0') to limit the range of voltages produced in the memory array's analog outputs. This narrower voltage range lets the system use simple, low-resolution analog-to-digital converters instead of expensive high-precision ones, dramatically cutting power consumption. The system further reduces overhead by skipping calculations that produce zero results and compressing data using bit-slice processing, which decreases memory and bandwidth demands while maintaining the energy benefits.
key_novelty: Fibonacci coding (a bit pattern constraint where every '1' is surrounded by '0's) shrinks the analog voltage range in the memory array, enabling lower-resolution analog-to-digital converters to replace energy-expensive high-precision ones.
contributions: Fibonacci-coded SRAM-based charge-domain CIM that reduces ADC voltage range
Zero-skipping methods to exploit bit-level sparsity and reduce ineffectual computation
Bit-slice compression to reduce memory capacity and bandwidth overhead
68.7% reduction in ADC energy with 3.48× energy efficiency improvement over TPUv4

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 68.7% ADC energy reduction, 3.48× energy efficiency vs TPUv4, 1.62× vs ISAAC

primary_theme: ADC energy optimization for compute-in-memory accelerators
